# Remotion 4.0.535 compatibility

Setup refuses an incompatible project and lists the complete required pins,
including the Remotion packages, React and React DOM. For an older
project, explicitly pin every listed dependency in `package.json`, review the
timing changes below, then rerun setup to install them and refresh the official
skills. No package-manager lockfile is required before setup: setup validates the
manifest, then runs npm install.

## Playback speed and loops

Since 4.0.530, `durationInFrames` selects the amount of child or media content
before `playbackRate` is applied. The visible duration in the parent timeline is
`durationInFrames / playbackRate`. This applies to sequences and audio/video
components; `trimBefore` advances the source start, and looping repeats the
selected range. The root composition's duration still sets the export length.
Audit nested speeds and loop boundaries when
upgrading existing compositions; do not multiply the root composition duration
automatically.

## WebM and constrained bitrate

For VP8, VP9 and AV1, setting `encodingBufferSize` also requires `videoBitrate`.
On the CLI, pair `--buffer-size` with `--video-bitrate`.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- When anything is spoken, offer an `.srt` in one line.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. Re-level with two-pass `loudnorm` (`TP=-1`, `linear=true`, the first pass's measured values) and review again before presenting.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

---
name: edit-in-remotion
description: "."
applications:
  - id: remotion
    role: primary
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
  craft: [rights-and-delivery]
---

Create one project per piece inside the active workspace, named for the piece:

```sh
voyager remotion setup ./<piece>/motion --json
```

Never add a piece to another piece's project; reuse a project only to revise its piece.

When the project has a selected brand kit (`brand/manifest.json`, with the kit in
`brand/BRAND.md`), read it as [brand-kit](../brand-kit/SKILL.md) describes
before designing any frame, and use its colours, fonts and logos.

The first setup can take several minutes, longest on Windows: it installs the npm
packages and downloads a ~95 MB browser. Setup has no background mode, so give the
command a shell timeout of at least 10 minutes. If setup is cut off anyway, run
the same command again: it discards the half-finished install and reinstalls,
reusing the packages it already downloaded.

When parsing JSON, read stdout only; do not merge stderr with `2>&1`.
Progress notices and live tool output go to stderr.

Setup installs Remotion 4.0.535, matching packages, official skills and Chrome
using Voyager's bundled runtime. Setup's JSON `skills` field is the absolute path
of the official skill router (`.../remotion-best-practices/SKILL.md`); open that
exact file and its relevant references. Its links are relative to that file's
folder; there is no `rules/` folder. Use them for Remotion craft; where their
preview, rendering or delivery workflow differs from Voyager's skills, follow
Voyager's skills: previews and stills are progress checks, not stopping points,
and a requested video is complete only when its full render, made with
`voyager remotion run`, is presented as the deliverable. If their download
failed, setup still succeeds with `skillsSkipped` and a warning instead of
`skills`: work without them; the next setup retries. Read [version compatibility](references/compatibility.md)
when upgrading a project, changing playback speed or exporting WebM.

Remotion bundles for Chrome 85, which rejects top-level `await`: never use it in
code Remotion bundles. The official local-fonts examples (`@remotion/fonts`)
`await loadFont(...)` at top level, alone or via `Promise.all`, and fail to
bundle. Instead, call `loadFont(...)` at module scope without `await`, once per
weight or style: it delays the render until the font is ready.

Run the official CLI through Voyager:

```sh
voyager remotion run ./<piece>/motion -- <Remotion CLI arguments>
```

For a standalone HTML preview, use `export-html`. It embeds only the `public/` files the code names; if the composition builds file names at runtime or lists files with `getStaticFiles()` and the export warns that files were left out, rerun with `--all-public`.

## Check stills and a short range

Render one frame, or a few seconds, without the full piece:

```sh
voyager remotion run ./<piece>/motion -- still src/index.tsx Motion out/check/scene2.png --frame=150
voyager remotion run ./<piece>/motion -- render src/index.tsx Motion out/check/move.mp4 --frames=150-240
```

Output paths are inside the project. Give each check a new versioned name
(`scene2_v2.png`, `move_v2.mp4`), never overwriting. Present the stills and ranges you look at with
`voyager files present PATH --deliverable none --json`, with a one-line
progress note that does not embed it (chat shows each as a card), and keep building without waiting for a reply.
Present final videos with `voyager files present PATH --deliverable "Piece" --json` rather than duplicating the card with an embed; re-presenting the same path reuses its record and shows the video again in this turn.

## Review the render

Whenever the user asks to check, review, QC or look at a render, or whether it
looks right, run `voyager media review` on it before any ffprobe or ffmpeg, and
list in `--sources` every recording, screenshot and image it shows, so footage
shown larger than its pixels is flagged (`checks.sourceScale`; a render has no
assemble recipe to read them from). Paths are relative to the render; `width`
and `height` are the size it reaches on screen at its deepest push-in, omitted
for the whole frame:

```sh
voyager media review ./<piece>/motion/out/final.mp4 --sources '[{"path":"../public/panel.mp4"},{"path":"../public/inset.png","width":2400,"height":1350}]'
```

On Windows/PowerShell, write that same source array to a UTF-8 `sources.json`
file and pass `--sources '@sources.json'` (or use the structured MCP media tool).
Use `--sources -` for piped JSON. Inline JSON can lose quotes in PowerShell;
the example above works on macOS/Linux.

A flagged source looks soft: use a sharper one, show it smaller, or zoom less.

To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [hosted media understanding](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).

## Verify delivery

Check the finished render with the full `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` already on your
PATH. Do not run ffmpeg through `voyager remotion run`: Remotion's own ffmpeg has
only a few filters (no `select`). To grab one frame of the render, use
`ffmpeg -ss <seconds> -i <video> -frames 1 <png>`.
